title: Clock and identity decision lab
description: Choose a generator condition to trace the allowed path. A safe response may reduce local availability, but it never issues an ID from an overlapping tuple.

nodes.label: Create caller
nodes.detail: Asks for an identifier. It can be routed to another healthy generator when this one fails closed.

nodes.label: Generator router
nodes.detail: Routes only to generators with a valid lease and healthy time status. It removes a quarantined process from the pool.

nodes.label: Identity lease
nodes.detail: Grants one generator identity to one live process and fences stale owners before a replacement can accept traffic.

nodes.label: Clock guard
nodes.detail: Compares wall time to the last emitted timestamp. It blocks generation when time regresses or the clock is untrusted.

nodes.label: Local generator
nodes.detail: Combines safe time, leased identity, and sequence in memory. It never calls a database to issue a normal ID.

nodes.label: Next-millisecond wait
nodes.detail: Holds only the overloaded generator after its sequence field is exhausted; the counter must not wrap in the same millisecond.

nodes.label: Quarantine and alert
nodes.detail: Removes an unsafe process from routing, preserves evidence, and requires an operator or automated recovery policy to make it safe again.

nodes.label: 64-bit ID
nodes.detail: Returns a positive integer whose timestamp, generator identity, and sequence form a unique tuple under the operating contract.

scenarios.label: Healthy issue
scenarios.summary: The process holds a valid identity lease, its clock is not behind its prior emission, and sequence capacity remains in the current millisecond.
scenarios.result: The generator packs the tuple and returns a local 64-bit ID without a request-time coordination call.

scenarios.label: Sequence exhausted
scenarios.summary: One generator has issued every sequence value for the current millisecond. Other healthy generators can still serve their own ranges.
scenarios.result: This generator waits for a later millisecond before emitting again. It must not wrap the sequence while timestamp and identity are unchanged.

scenarios.label: Clock rollback
scenarios.summary: The wall clock is earlier than the last timestamp this process emitted, perhaps after a VM resume or time correction.
scenarios.result: Generation stops and routing removes this process. A retry can reach another healthy generator; this one remains unavailable until its time is safe.

scenarios.label: Duplicate identity attempt
scenarios.summary: A replacement is starting while a stale process still appears to hold the same generator identity. The lease service detects incompatible ownership.
scenarios.result: The system fences and drains the stale owner before the replacement becomes routable. Allowing both processes to issue IDs would violate uniqueness.
